approved_translation: Do not panic over imagined dangers; investigate before you flee, for fear is contagious.
translation_author: Ellen C. Babbitt (retold from traditional sources)
context_summary: Once upon a time, a Rabbit was asleep under a palm-tree. All at once he woke up, and thought: "What if the world should break up! You foolish Rabbit!" And the Lion ran back to the other animals, and told them all about it. If it had not been for the wise King of Beasts, they might be running still.
interpretation_boundaries: Do not depict specific historical Buddha figures — keep characters as generic animals or people
Focus on the moral lesson, avoid doctrinal Buddhist claims
Keep animal characters naturalistic, not anthropomorphic
